summary: The shifted endpoints lie in the stated source metronoids, have the labelled atom as their exact midpoint, and allow every atom in a closed halfspace to be charged once to a physical source. The aggregate charge at each source is at most d_z(s) and hence beta_z, so the metronoid halfspace bound proves domination without pooling target-fiber densities; the argument also handles coincident atoms, distinct labels over one target, boundary points, and proper or degenerate fiber sections. The support, intrinsic residual ranks, fixed-target submeasure and multiplicity bound, B_g and O_g comparisons, strict hard-constant calculations, numerical gamma_d bound, and single-measure D accounting are all correct.
